finding.claim: With a ClientCredentialsProvider, any 401 from the configured MCP endpoint lets the server choose the authorization server via resource_metadata, causing the stored client_id and client_secret to be sent via Basic auth to an attacker-chosen token endpoint without user interaction.
finding.source: HTTP 401 WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata parameter from the MCP endpoint (lib/mcp/client/oauth/discovery.rb:71, lib/mcp/client/http.rb:416)
finding.sink: post_to_token_endpoint Basic auth header and form POST (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:696, 707)

trace.note: resource_metadata read from raw WWW-Authenticate header
ensure_secure_url! only enforces https or loopback
issuer check compares against attacker-controlled discovery URL
client_credentials branch taken with no user interaction
client_secret sent in Basic auth header

finding.guards_checked: ensure_secure_url! (https or loopback) on PRM URL, AS, and endpoints; issuer equality check (attacker controls both sides); resource_covers? only when PRM includes resource (attacker can omit); OAuthURLGuard only applies to MCP-endpoint requests, token POST uses a separate plain Faraday client (flow.rb:791-794); no AS pinning across re-authorization. Legacy path (flow.rb:240-242, 254-259) also lets the MCP origin's own AS metadata name an arbitrary https token_endpoint with no issuer check.

finding.claim: On any 401 after a prior grant, the stored refresh_token and client_secret are silently POSTed to an authorization server chosen by the server's resource_metadata URL, without re-verifying the AS that issued the refresh token.
finding.source: HTTP 401 WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata parameter from the MCP endpoint (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:416, 418)
finding.sink: exchange_refresh_token form body and post_to_token_endpoint Basic auth (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:178-183, 661-669, 696)

trace.note: attempt_refresh runs first with attacker-supplied resource_metadata
refresh! re-discovers PRM and AS from attacker URL
client_secret sent via Basic auth to attacker token_endpoint

finding.guards_checked: Same HTTPS/loopback and issuer checks as finding 1; no check that the refreshing AS matches the AS that issued the refresh token; no user consent on this path. Failed refresh falls through to full flow, but the credentials have already been sent.
